parsed.evidence: All 20 top crops center on a tire under its wheel-well arch, across many vehicle types and colours (grayscale keeps 93%), while random non-vehicle photos score 1-3. parsed.explanation: The unit responds to vehicle wheels seen from the side together with the curved wheel arch or fender around them, on cars, vans, buses, trucks and fire engines, in their usual upright orientation.
parsed.evidence: All 20 top crops are centred on a tyre and rim inside a wheel well, across many vehicle types and colours, and random photos score at most 3. parsed.explanation: The unit detects a vehicle wheel sitting under its wheel arch: a round tire/hub inside the curved fender opening, seen from the side and upright.

parsed.explanation: The unit detects the front wheel of a road vehicle, meaning the tyre and hub framed by the arch of the wheel well, seen from the side and upright. It responds weakly to other upright round or arched shapes such as bicycle wheels, tractor wheels and round metal objects.
parsed.evidence: All 20 top crops are a vehicle wheel under its fender arch, across cars, trucks, buses and fire engines in many colours, and grayscale keeps 93% of the activation. parsed.missing_data: Synthetic tests of an isolated wheel versus an arch without a wheel, plus rotated wheels, would show whether the fender arch is required.

CPS_s2.explanation: Responds to the wheel of a road vehicle sitting in its wheel arch, i.e. the tire/rim together with the curved fender edge above it, seen upright from the side or at a three-quarter angle.

parsed.explanation: Responds to the wheel of a road vehicle sitting in its wheel arch, i.e. the tire/rim together with the curved fender edge above it, seen upright from the side or at a three-quarter angle.
parsed.evidence: All 20 top crops center on a wheel under an arched fender across cars, trucks, buses, and emergency vehicles of many colours. The unit is colour-invariant (grayscale keeps 93%) but loses almost everything under rotate_90, edge_map, and phase scramble (percentiles 0–7), and weaker activations reach bicycle/tractor wheels (4–5) and only round or curved non-vehicle objects at 1–3.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on isolated wheels with no fender, versus empty wheel arches or other round arched shapes, would separate a wheel detector from a wheel-plus-arch conjunction.

CPS_s3.explanation: The unit detects a road-vehicle wheel seen in side view together with the arched wheel well or fender above it, on cars, vans, buses, trucks and fire engines. It responds weakly to other circular rims or bosses, such as bicycle and tractor wheels, coins and ornate circular metalwork.

parsed.explanation: The unit detects a road-vehicle wheel seen in side view together with the arched wheel well or fender above it, on cars, vans, buses, trucks and fire engines. It responds weakly to other circular rims or bosses, such as bicycle and tractor wheels, coins and ornate circular metalwork.
parsed.evidence: All 20 top crops are centered on a tire plus the fender arch above it, across many vehicle types and colors (grayscale keeps 93%), and random photos without vehicles score only 1-3. The unit is very sensitive to orientation (rotate_90 keeps 23%, percentile 0), phase scrambling (1%) and edge maps (13%), which fits an upright wheel-in-arch shape rather than a texture or color.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on isolated wheels without bodywork and on empty wheel arches, to tell whether the tire, the arch or the combination drives the response.
